claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm enquiring about my one child - their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about Child Benefit for Alex.

To help me assess your eligibility, I need to ask: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to understand their current situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, are they at school, college, university, or doing an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They left school and they're working now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more important question:

**How many hours per week is Alex working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex works full-time - it's at the local supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation: Since Alex is 17 years old and has left education or training to work full-time, Child Benefit eligibility stops. According to the rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Full-time work at a supermarket would typically exceed 24 hours per week, which means Child Benefit would no longer be payable for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

The key reason is that Alex has stopped being in approved education or training and is now working full-time. The rules state that Child Benefit stops when a young person starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training—which applies to Alex's situation.

If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if they return to approved education or training), please let me know.

According to the Child Benefit rules, payments stop if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training. Therefore, Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit.
